content: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, avoid using strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Monitor the patient closely. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates cannot be avoided, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive substrate as per prescribing guidelines. Clarithromycin increases the effects of bemiparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor the patient closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of berotralstat via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of betrixaban via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. If coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor, reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily. Monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the effects of bivalirudin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bromocriptine by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing elimination. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels of cabergoline by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required, reduce the cabozantinib dose and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may alter vitamin D metabolism, requiring dose adjustments and close monitoring of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium levels. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of calcitriol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor plasma levels closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Dose reduction of cariprazine is required when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefdinir, cefditoren, cefoxitin, cefpodoxime, and cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and chlorpromazine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and cholera vaccine exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received systemic antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Avoid concomitant use of bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors. Monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin if coadministration is necessary. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ciclesonide (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and cisapride both increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. Clarithromycin and citalopram both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for QT prolongation or ventricular tachyarrhythmias. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of clevidipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Clarithromycin and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
